Back Cover / 封底

ISBN: 978-1-098-14689-4. US $69.99 · CAN $87.99. Category: Cloud Computing.

ISBN：978-1-098-14689-4。美国定价 69.99 美元 · 加拿大 87.99 加元。分类：云计算。

Enterprises building complex and large-scale applications in the cloud face multiple challenges. Nearly every decision, from figuring out the right tools to estimating the right provisioning, poses a complicated set of choices and trade-offs. System design gives you the ability to build and scale these applications, and this practical guide helps you decide which pieces to use and how to fit them together. Authors Jayanth Kumar and Mandeep Singh equip software architects and engineers with essential AWS and system design knowledge to help you make good decisions and overcome the challenges of designing and scaling enterprise software architecture.

在云端构建复杂、大规模应用的企业面临着多重挑战。几乎每一个决策——从挑选合适的工具到估算恰当的资源预置——都伴随着复杂的选择与取舍。系统设计赋予你构建和扩展这些应用的能力，而这本实用指南帮助你决定使用哪些部件、以及如何把它们拼装起来。作者 Jayanth Kumar 和 Mandeep Singh 为软件架构师和工程师配备了必备的 AWS 与系统设计知识，帮助你做出好决策，克服设计与扩展企业级软件架构时遇到的挑战。

  • Learn the basics and best practices of successful system design.
    学习成功系统设计的基础与最佳实践。
  • Understand key AWS services and their strengths and limitations for building large-scale systems.
    理解关键 AWS 服务，以及它们在构建大规模系统时的优势与局限。
  • Examine engineering patterns and principles that best support large-scale systems, and learn how to design architecture with scalability, operations, and resilience in mind.
    审视最能支撑大规模系统的工程模式与原则，并学习在设计架构时把可扩展性、运维和韧性考虑在内。
  • Learn what highly performant and cost-optimized architectures look like on AWS and the tools and frameworks that are best for specific use cases.
    了解在 AWS 上高性能、成本优化的架构长什么样，以及哪些工具和框架最适合特定用例。

Part I. System Design Basics / 第一部分：系统设计基础

  • Chapter 1. System Design Trade-offs and Guidelines (p.5) — 系统设计的取舍与准则
    System Design Concepts; Communication; Consistency; Availability; Reliability; Scalability; Maintainability; Fault Tolerance; Fallacies of Distributed Computing; System Design Trade-offs (Time vs. Space, Latency vs. Throughput, Performance vs. Scalability, Consistency vs. Availability); System Design Guidelines; Conclusion.
  • Chapter 2. Storage Types and Relational Stores (p.35) — 存储类型与关系型存储
    Data Storage Format (File/Block/Object-Based Storage); Relational Databases; Relational Database Concepts; RDBMS Architecture; Optimizing Relational Databases; Scaling Relational Databases; Open Source RDBMSs; Conclusion.
  • Chapter 3. Nonrelational Stores (p.67) — 非关系型存储
    Nonrelational Database Concepts; Key-Value Databases; Document Databases; Columnar Databases; Graph Databases; Conclusion.
  • Chapter 4. Caching Policies and Strategies (p.95) — 缓存策略与方针
    Benefits of Caching; Cache Eviction Policies; Cache Invalidation; Caching Strategies; Cache Deployment; Caching Mechanisms; Content Delivery Networks; Open Source Caching Solutions (Memcached, Redis); Conclusion.
  • Chapter 5. Load Balancing Approaches and Techniques (p.119) — 负载均衡方法与技术
    Networking Components; Benefits of Load Balancing; LB Deployment and Placement; Load Balancing Algorithms; Session Persistence; Types of Load Balancers; Nginx; Conclusion.
  • Chapter 6. Communication Networks and Protocols (p.137) — 通信网络与协议
    OSI Model; TCP/IP Model; Communication Types (HTTP Polling, WebSockets, SSE); Remote Procedure Call; REST; GraphQL; WebRTC; Conclusion.

    Evolution of Application Deployment; Containerization (Docker); Container Orchestration; Container Deployment Strategies; CI/CD Pipeline with Gitflow; Monitoring and Incident Management; Conclusion.

Foreword / 前言

Systems design is one of the most important aspects of building apps that are scalable, available, performant, and secure, even when your usage increases by an order of magnitude or two. That’s why I found the topic of this book to be so important. I like that this book starts with covering the basics of trade-offs in distributed systems, such as the CAP theorem, units of blast radius, and other common trade-offs in systems design, and then moves to how to apply these principles in practice. I found this approach—going from core principles to actually putting them into practice on critical design decisions (such as “What is the best database for running my workload?” and “What’s the best caching strategy for my workloads?” and “Which storage service should I choose?”)—to be especially helpful as it teaches people how to think about these problems even as new capabilities from AWS emerge, making the concepts in this book more durable.

系统设计是构建可扩展、可用、高性能且安全的应用时最重要的方面之一——即便你的使用量增长一两个数量级也是如此。这就是为什么我觉得这本书的主题如此重要。我很欣赏这本书从分布式系统中各种取舍的基础讲起，例如 CAP 定理、爆炸半径（blast radius）的单位、以及系统设计中其他常见的取舍，然后再转向如何在实践中应用这些原则。我发现这种做法——从核心原理出发，再到把它们真正落到关键设计决策上（比如“运行我的负载最好的数据库是什么？”“我的负载最好的缓存策略是什么？”“我该选哪种存储服务？”）——特别有帮助，因为它教会人们如何思考这类问题，哪怕 AWS 不断推出新能力，这本书里的概念也依然经得起时间考验。

Personally, reading this book reminded me so much of the early days of AWS, when we spent a lot of time discussing these trade-offs. At that time, concepts like CAP theorem, blast radius, and seamless scalability were not well understood, and we had robust discussions around these topics and the inherent trade-offs they come with. However, those discussions led to some incredibly robust AWS services, such as S3, DynamoDB, and many others that millions of AWS customers love. I hope that you grasp these concepts and are inspired to build similarly amazing products and services that delight their customers.

就我个人而言，读这本书让我想起 AWS 的早期岁月，那时我们花大量时间讨论这些取舍。当时，像 CAP 定理、爆炸半径、无缝可扩展性这样的概念还没有被很好地理解，我们围绕这些话题及其固有的取舍进行了充分的讨论。然而，正是那些讨论催生了一些极其稳健的 AWS 服务，例如 S3、DynamoDB 以及其他数百万 AWS 客户所喜爱的服务。我希望你能掌握这些概念，并受到启发，去构建同样令人惊叹、能让客户满意的产品和服务。

Congratulations to the authors for writing such an excellent book, and best of luck to all who embark on this journey!

祝贺作者写出如此出色的书，也祝所有踏上这趟旅程的人好运！

— Swami Sivasubramanian, Vice President, AI and Data at AWS

——Swami Sivasubramanian，AWS 人工智能与数据副总裁

Preface / 序言

System design is a disciplined art, so let’s create some large-scale masterpieces.

系统设计是一门讲究章法的艺术，那么就让我们创作一些大规模的杰作吧。

System Design on AWS is a comprehensive guide to helping software architects and engineers understand, build, and scale complex systems on the Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud. The book provides a structured approach to tackling real-world system design challenges on AWS in a continuously evolving cloud landscape. The material focuses on fundamental principles, architectural trade-offs, and practical use cases, guiding you from Day 0 (minimum viable product) to Day N (most valuable product). Through detailed chapters, this book demystifies AWS’s wide-ranging services and how they can be strategically leveraged to address both technical and business requirements.

《System Design on AWS》是一本全面的指南，帮助软件架构师和工程师在 Amazon Web Services（AWS）云上理解、构建并扩展复杂系统。本书提供了一套结构化方法，在不断演进的云环境中应对 AWS 上真实世界的系统设计挑战。内容聚焦于基础原理、架构取舍和实用用例，引导你从第 0 天（最小可行产品）走到第 N 天（最有价值产品）。通过详尽的章节，本书揭开 AWS 众多服务的神秘面纱，并说明如何战略性地利用它们来同时满足技术与业务需求。

How This Book Is Organized / 本书的结构

Organized into three core parts, this book begins by establishing a foundation in system design, then dives into the essential AWS services for building resilient architectures, and concludes with practical system design use cases. Foundational system design patterns, scaling mechanisms, caching strategies, network protocols, and deployment strategies are covered. By exploring these elements in a cloud context, the book offers a toolkit for approaching and solving large-scale design problems in any industry. Each part opener breaks down the chapters included in that part, so take a look at those openers for details. This book aims to equip you with:

本书分为三个核心部分：首先打下系统设计的基础，然后深入讲解构建弹性架构所必需的 AWS 服务，最后以实用的系统设计用例收尾。内容涵盖基础系统设计模式、扩展机制、缓存策略、网络协议和部署策略。通过在云的语境下探讨这些要素，本书提供了一套工具箱，用于在任何行业中处理和解决大规模设计问题。每个部分的开篇都会拆解该部分所包含的章节，细节请参看那些开篇。本书旨在让你具备：

  • A solid understanding of fundamental system design principles and trade-offs
    对系统设计基本原理与取舍的扎实理解
  • Proficiency in key AWS services and their roles in building large-scale systems
    熟练掌握关键 AWS 服务及其在构建大规模系统中的角色
  • Insight into real-world use cases that illustrate how to structure and deploy scalable architectures on AWS
    洞察真实世界用例，了解如何在 AWS 上构建并部署可扩展架构
  • Strategies to balance performance, scalability, and cost in AWS cloud environments
    在 AWS 云环境中平衡性能、可扩展性与成本的策略
Page 17

What This Book Isn’t / 本书不做什么

This book does not provide detailed code implementations for deploying the infrastructure or application business logic. Instead, it emphasizes the architecture and design process, helping you understand how to break a system down into manageable components and make informed architectural decisions.

本书并不提供部署基础设施或应用业务逻辑的详细代码实现。相反，它强调架构与设计过程，帮助你理解如何把一个系统拆分成可管理的组件，并做出明智的架构决策。

Who Should Read This Book / 谁应该读这本书

This book is ideal for software architects, developers, DevOps engineers, and system architects who want to build or scale applications on AWS. It is especially useful for professionals transitioning from on-premises to cloud infrastructure or aiming to leverage AWS for large-scale applications. A basic understanding of software implementation and familiarity with one programming language are recommended.

本书非常适合希望在 AWS 上构建或扩展应用的软件架构师、开发人员、DevOps 工程师和系统架构师。对于那些从本地基础设施迁移到云、或希望利用 AWS 构建大规模应用的专业人士尤其有用。建议具备软件实现的基础理解，并熟悉至少一门编程语言。

This book is also recommended for people holding leadership positions in software development and DevOps. The guidance and principles in the book will help you remove team blockers while building systems and making informed decisions.

本书也推荐给在软件开发和 DevOps 中担任领导岗位的人。书中的指导和原则会帮助你在构建系统、做出明智决策时清除团队的障碍。

While this book is titled System Design on AWS and the focus is on the AWS cloud, we recommend it to everyone who loves to build systems on any of the cloud providers’ platforms or for on-premises data centers as well as anyone who is just curious about building systems. The design and scaling principles discussed in the book are agnostic of cloud providers.

虽然本书名为《System Design on AWS》且聚焦于 AWS 云，但我们把它推荐给所有喜欢在任何云厂商平台或本地数据中心上构建系统的人，以及任何只是对构建系统感到好奇的人。书中讨论的设计与扩展原则并不绑定于任何特定云厂商。

Conventions Used in This Book / 本书使用的排版约定

The following typographical conventions are used in this book: Italic indicates new terms, URLs, email addresses, filenames, and file extensions. Constant width is used for program listings, as well as within paragraphs to refer to program elements such as variable or function names, databases, data types, environment variables, statements, and keywords. Constant width bold shows commands or other text that should be typed literally by the user. Constant width italic shows text that should be replaced with user-supplied values or by values determined by context.

本书使用以下排版约定：斜体表示新术语、URL、电子邮箱地址、文件名和文件扩展名。等宽字体用于程序清单，以及在段落中指代程序元素，例如变量名或函数名、数据库、数据类型、环境变量、语句和关键字。等宽粗体显示用户应原样键入的命令或其他文本。等宽斜体显示应由用户提供的值或由上下文确定的值来替换的文本。

PART I

System Design Basics

第一部分：系统设计基础

“Perfection is finally attained not when there is no longer anything to add but when there is no longer anything to take away.” — Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
“完美的达成，最终不在于无可增添，而在于无可删减。”——安托万·德·圣埃克苏佩里

The first part of this book will give you a solid foundation in system design, offering insights into the fundamental principles that underpin all types of software systems, ranging from trade-offs to the criteria for picking the right tools and technologies and thus, the right architecture patterns.

本书第一部分将为你打下系统设计的坚实基础，带你理解支撑各类软件系统的基本原理——从各种取舍，到挑选合适工具与技术（进而挑选合适架构模式）的评判标准。

In Part I, you will:

在第一部分中，你将：

  • Grasp the system trade-offs inherent in large-scale distributed systems and know how to balance conflicting demands like scalability, reliability, and maintainability
    把握大规模分布式系统中固有的系统取舍，并懂得如何平衡可扩展性、可靠性和可维护性等相互冲突的需求
  • Develop a clear understanding of options for data storage, including file, block, and object stores, alongside relational and nonrelational databases and methods for scaling them
    清晰理解数据存储的各种选择，包括文件、块、对象存储，以及关系型与非关系型数据库及其扩展方法
  • Master techniques to achieve low latency and high throughput in storage and compute through caching and content delivery networks (CDNs)
    掌握通过缓存和内容分发网络（CDN）在存储与计算中实现低延迟、高吞吐的技术
  • Learn to horizontally scale systems with load balancers, API gateways, and reverse proxies
    学会用负载均衡器、API 网关和反向代理对系统做水平扩展
  • Navigate the choices among communication and network protocols at different layers of the OSI and TCP/IP models and know how to choose when to use what
    在 OSI 与 TCP/IP 模型各层的通信与网络协议之间做出选择，并知道何时该用哪种
Page 23
  • Familiarize yourself with the system design architecture patterns that are commonly used in the industry and learn how to adapt them to various system requirements
    熟悉业界常用的系统设计架构模式，并学习如何根据各种系统需求对它们加以改造
  • Gain insight into the AWS services that map to different system design paradigms, which we will explore further in later chapters
    洞察与不同系统设计范式相对应的 AWS 服务，我们将在后续章节进一步探讨

Chapter 1 will delve into the world of trade-offs in large-scale distributed systems. We’ll explore essential concepts like reliability, scalability, and maintainability, shedding light on why these trade-offs emerge. We’ll tackle common misconceptions through the fallacies of distributed computing and address pivotal choices such as space versus time, latency versus throughput, performance versus scalability, and consistency versus availability. We’ll also offer practical guidelines and strategies that have emerged from years of system design wisdom, providing tangible approaches to enhance system performance and efficiency.

第 1 章将深入大规模分布式系统中取舍的世界。我们会探讨可靠性、可扩展性、可维护性等基本概念，阐明这些取舍为何会出现。我们会通过分布式计算谬误来纠正常见误解，并讨论空间与时间、延迟与吞吐、性能与可扩展性、一致性与可用性等关键抉择。我们还会给出从多年系统设计智慧中沉淀出的实用准则与策略，提供切实可行的方法来提升系统性能与效率。

Chapter 2 will introduce you to different types of data storage, including file, block, and object stores. We’ll cover relational databases, their concepts, and their architecture in this chapter. You’ll gain insights into the intricacies of scaling and optimizing relational databases, including techniques like partitioning, indexing, replication, federation, sharding, and denormalization.

第 2 章将向你介绍不同类型的数据存储，包括文件、块和对象存储。本章会讲解关系数据库及其概念与架构。你将深入理解扩展和优化关系数据库的复杂细节，包括分区、索引、复制、联邦、分片和反规范化等技术。

Chapter 3 will unveil the architecture of nonrelational databases, such as key-value, wide-column, document, and graph databases, and discuss how leaderless architectures enable scalability through mechanisms like quorum-based replication, consistent hashing, and eventual consistency.

第 3 章将揭示非关系数据库的架构，例如键值、宽列、文档和图数据库，并讨论无主架构如何基于仲裁复制、一致性哈希和最终一致性等机制实现可扩展性。

Chapter 4 will introduce you to caching, where we will explore diverse caching strategies spanning different tiers, from client and server to application and database levels. We’ll dissect core caching approaches like write-through, read-through, refresh-ahead, write-back, and cache-aside. Moreover, we’ll unravel the potential of both push and pull CDNs in reducing latency and improving the efficiency of content delivery.

第 4 章将向你介绍缓存，我们会探讨跨越多层的各种缓存策略——从客户端、服务器到应用层和数据库层。我们会剖析 write-through、read-through、refresh-ahead、write-back 和 cache-aside 等核心缓存方式。此外，我们还会揭示推（push）CDN 与拉（pull）CDN 在降低延迟、提升内容分发效率方面的潜力。

Chapter 5 will explore load balancers, API gateways, and reverse proxies, and includes discussions on Layer 4 (L4) network scaling and Layer 7 (L7) application layer scaling. Concepts like sticky sessions, forward proxies, and reverse proxies will come to life as we delve into the nuances of creating scalable, resilient architectures.

第 5 章将探讨负载均衡器、API 网关和反向代理，并讨论四层（L4）网络扩展和七层（L7）应用层扩展。当我们深入创建可扩展、有韧性架构的细微之处时，粘性会话、正向代理和反向代理等概念将变得鲜活起来。

Chapter 6 will demystify network protocols, unraveling the intricacies of TCP/IP and User Datagram Protocol (UDP), as well as HTTP, SMTP, Extensible Messaging and Presence Protocol (XMPP), and their suitable applications. You’ll gain a comprehensive understanding of synchronous and asynchronous service design and delve into standards like REST, WebRTC, and GraphQL. Mastering these communication concepts will better equip you to make informed choices for different use cases.

第 6 章将揭开网络协议的神秘面纱，梳理 TCP/IP 与用户数据报协议（UDP）以及 HTTP、SMTP、可扩展消息与存在协议（XMPP）的复杂细节及其适用场景。你将全面理解同步与异步服务设计，并深入 REST、WebRTC、GraphQL 等标准。掌握这些通信概念，能让你更好地为不同用例做出明智选择。

Page 24

Chapter 7 is all about containerization: the creation, management, and orchestration of Docker containers. You’ll also be introduced to modern strategies for container deployment, enabling you to manage the complexity of modern cloud native applications.

第 7 章全部关于容器化：Docker 容器的创建、管理和编排。你还会接触到现代容器部署策略，从而能够管理现代云原生应用的复杂性。

Chapter 8 will cover different architectural designs and patterns, starting with choreography and orchestration in detail, where we explore asynchronous architectures, message brokers, message queues, and publisher-subscriber patterns. As you delve deeper into large-scale software engineering design, you’ll compare microservices with monolithic designs, serverless architecture, the saga pattern, the event-sourcing pattern, big data architectures, and domain-driven design.

第 8 章将讲解不同的架构设计与模式，首先详细讲编排（choreography）与协调（orchestration），探讨异步架构、消息代理、消息队列和发布-订阅模式。随着你深入大规模软件工程设计，你会把微服务与单体设计、无服务器架构、saga 模式、事件溯源模式、大数据架构和领域驱动设计加以比较。

After this comprehensive journey through the nuances of system design in Part I, you’ll be well prepared to wield these principles and technologies in creating effective and efficient large-scale systems. Part II will cover the AWS services in detail, bringing these concepts to light in their use and trade-offs in cloud architecture.

在走完第一部分这趟贯穿系统设计细微之处的综合旅程之后，你将做好充分准备，运用这些原理和技术去创建有效而高效的大规模系统。第二部分将详细讲解 AWS 服务，在云架构的使用与取舍中把这些概念落到实处。
